evidence: pkg/expr/reader.go:129-131 returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") when the SQL query type is read. It does use fmt.Errorf with a lowercase message like the other branches (reader.go:56, 87, 100, 181), so the 'inconsistent' part doesn't hold. 'not implemented' also matches the existing wording for unsupported commands (nodes.go:162: "... not implemented"). This PR is a CVE-2024-9264 hotfix, and saying 'not implemented' is a deliberate way to turn the feature off without explaining why. A message like 'SQL expressions are disabled' would be a bit clearer for users, but that is wording, not a defect.

pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200: `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` inverts the flag, and then both branches return false. The function always returns false, the flag lookup does nothing, and the variable name says the opposite of what it holds. The behavior is what this security fix wants (SQL is always off), so this is a readability/maintenance problem, not a runtime bug. Simplifying to `return false`, or adding a comment saying the function is hard-disabled because of the CVE, would make the intent clear.

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-22: every DB method returns errors.New("not implemented"). The misclassification is real. On the legacy path (when expressionParser is off, nodes.go:159-160 calls UnmarshalSQLCommand), the reader.go gate is skipped. NewSQLCommand (sql_command.go:30-35) then gets the error from TablesList, logs 'invalid sql query', and returns BadRequest 'sql-invalid-sql' / 'error reading SQL command'. A sentinel ErrSQLExpressionsDisabled would only help if NewSQLCommand also checked for it with errors.Is, so the sentinel alone isn't enough. A simpler fix is to gate at NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand. Low impact: the feature is off either way and users just see a misleading message.

pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-29: TablesList calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, which always fails (db.go:16-18). It wraps that as 'error serializing sql' and logs it at Error level. sql_command.go:31-35 then turns it into BadRequest 'sql-invalid-sql'. That path is reachable without the reader.go gate via nodes.go:159-160 (legacy, non-expressionParser path; grep shows it is the only other caller of NewSQLCommand). So SQL expressions show up as 'invalid SQL' rather than 'disabled'. The variable name `duckDB` (parser.go:23) is also stale now that the go-duck import is removed. Both are minor; behavior is still safe (SQL never runs).

pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-100: Execute calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto, which always returns 'not implemented' (db.go:20-22). In practice Execute can't be reached. A SQLCommand is only built through NewSQLCommand (sql_command.go:25), which always fails at TablesList (sql_command.go:30-35, parser.go:26) before a command object exists, and the reader path is also gated at reader.go:129-131. So the requested 'fail fast' already happens at construction. If Execute were somehow reached, it puts the error in rsp.Error (sql_command.go:101-104) and does not crash. No change is needed for safety; the only remaining point is the message wording covered in issues 2/3.
